items.title: Cherubim as guardians and biblical sacred-space figures
items.claim_text: Genesis 3:24 stations cherubim east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life. Later biblical sanctuary texts place cherubim over or within sacred settings; Genesis 3 does not describe their physical appearance.
items.description: Genesis 3:24 stations cherubim east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life. Later biblical sanctuary texts place cherubim over or within sacred settings; Genesis 3 does not describe their physical appearance.

bibliographic_details.notes: Primary biblical text.

bibliographic_details.title: Cherubim
bibliographic_details.publisher: The Lexham Bible Dictionary; Lexham Press
bibliographic_details.locator: Entry “Cherubim,” especially Genesis 3:24 and biblical sanctuary/throne references
bibliographic_details.notes: Reference entry on cherubim as guardians of sacred space and their biblical sanctuary/throne associations; Genesis gives no visual description.

rationale.notes: Comparative biblical sanctuary context (not Genesis applicability anchors): Exodus 25:18–22 places cherubim over the ark; 1 Kings 6:23–35 describes cherubim in the temple. These later texts contextualize Genesis 3:24 but do not establish a single physical appearance for Eden’s cherubim. Comparative Scripture sources retained: g1-exodus-text and g1-kings-text; scholarly context source retained: g1-lexham-cherubim.
rationale.confidence_rationale: Genesis’s guarding role is explicit; the wider biblical sacred-space pattern is comparative context.
rationale.passage_relevance: Genesis 3:24 stations cherubim east of the garden to guard the way to the tree of life. Later biblical sanctuary texts place cherubim over or within sacred settings; Genesis 3 does not describe their physical appearance. This supports passage-specific synthesis of Genesis 3 while preserving the stated limits.
rationale.scholarly_interpretation: Lexham’s entry discusses guardian and sanctuary/throne associations. This context excludes later popular “baby angel” imagery but does not establish a single appearance for Genesis 3.
rationale.primary_observation: Genesis gives the cherubim a guarding function; Exodus 25:18–22 and 1 Kings 6:23–35 provide later sanctuary context.
